checks_run.procedure: The same two session-end probes on a stack with the product's DEFAULT rate limits (with-stack-default-limits.sh: AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE and RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE unset, so 20 and 300). Round 13 locked out the IP here. PACE_MS=62000 waits before each trigger, so my probe's own sign-ins stay inside the 20/min auth budget.
checks_run.environment: fresh disposable stack with default rate limits; Chromium; Node 24.21.0
checks_run.expected: as DOM-R14-12, and no 429 or IP lock-out
checks_run.actual:
Final run: r13 4/4 and r14 31/31, exit 0, EXIT=0. Every trigger in EN and AR made 1 /me, got 0 429s and landed once on sign-in with the message. The second context signed in and the user returned to the page.
Attempt 1 (stack-run-5-attempt1; r14-session-end-ui-default-limits-attempt1, exit 1):
- The first four EN triggers passed, each with 1 /me and no 429.
- Then en.absolute-expiry.other-context-signs-in and en.absolute-expiry.sign-in-returns FAILED, and the next sign-in crashed waiting for the form.
- Cause: my probe's own volume against the per-IP auth budget. Each form sign-in costs two auth requests (the dev-login availability probe and the POST), the probe signs in about three times per trigger, and the r13 probe ran just before. Once the budget is exhausted, the dev form is hidden, by the pre-existing LoginPage design (dev mode only).
- The session-end handling itself used 1 /me per trigger. Pacing removed the failure.
The r13 probe in attempt 1 passed 4/4.
